questions.question: In a maximum flow problem on a directed network with source $S$ and sink $T$, $x_{ij}$ is the flow on edge $i\to j$ and $c_{ij}$ its capacity. Which conditions make the flows $x_{ij}$ feasible?
options: $0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$, and inflow equals outflow at every vertex including $S$ and $T$.
$x_{ij}=c_{ij}$ on every edge, and inflow equals outflow at all vertices except $S$ and $T$.
$0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$, and inflow equals outflow at all vertices except $S$ and $T$.
$0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$, and every edge carries the same amount of flow.

questions.question: A maximum flow problem has source $S$, with only outgoing edges, and sink $T$, with only incoming edges, and requires inflow to equal outflow at every other vertex. Why is this balance not also required at $S$ and $T$?
options: Because $S$ and $T$ have no capacities to respect.
Because the sink may store at most the capacity of its edges.
At $S$ it would force all outflow to 0: $S$ has no inflow.
Because flow at $S$ and $T$ is irrelevant for the objective.

questions.question: In a flow network with source $S$ and sink $T$, a feasible flow keeps every edge flow between 0 and its capacity and balances inflow and outflow at each intermediate vertex. Why is the total outflow of $S$ then equal to the total inflow of $T$?
options: It holds only for a maximum flow, not for every feasible flow.
Because the capacities out of $S$ equal those into $T$.
Because every edge carries the same flow from $S$ to $T$.
Each intermediate vertex passes on exactly what it receives.

questions.question: For a directed network with source $S$, sink $T$ and edge capacities $c_{ij}\ge0$, consider the flow with $x_{ij}=0$ on every edge $i\to j$. Feasibility requires $0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$ and conservation at every vertex other than $S$ and $T$. Is this flow feasible?
options: Yes; it meets all constraints, with flow value 0.
No, because some capacity must be used.
No, because inflow at $T$ must be positive.
Only if the network has no route from $S$ to $T$.

questions.question: In a maximum flow problem, $x_{ij}$ is the flow on edge $i\to j$ with capacity $c_{ij}$. The network has an edge $A\to B$ but no edge $B\to A$. A planner wants to send 2 units from $B$ to $A$ by setting $x_{AB}=-2$. Is this allowed?
options: Yes; a negative flow simply runs along the edge in reverse.
Yes, provided $|x_{AB}|\le c_{AB}$ still holds.
Yes, because edges of a flow network can be used both ways.
No; $x_{AB}\ge0$, so flow runs only from $A$ to $B$.

questions.question: In a flow network, vertex $B$ is neither source nor sink. Its incoming edges carry $x_{AB}=3$ and $x_{SB}=4$, and its outgoing edges are $B\to T$ with $x_{BT}=5$ and $B\to C$. What must $x_{BC}$ be?
A flow network has source $S$ and sink $T$ and edges with flow/capacity $S\to A$: 3/4, $S\to B$: 4/5, $A\to T$: 2/3, $A\to B$: 1/2 and $B\to T$: 5/6. The flow is feasible. What is its flow value?
A flow network has edges with flow/capacity $S\to A$: 5/4, $S\to B$: 2/3, $A\to B$: 1/2, $A\to T$: 4/5 and $B\to T$: 3/4, with source $S$ and sink $T$. Which assessment of this flow is correct?
options: Feasible: inflow equals outflow at both $A$ and $B$.
Infeasible: inflow and outflow differ at the source $S$.
Infeasible: edge $S\to A$ carries more than its capacity 4.
Infeasible: edge $B\to T$ is used below its capacity.

questions.question: A flow network with source $S$ and sink $T$ has capacities $S\to A$: 4, $S\to B$: 3, $A\to B$: 2, $A\to T$: 3 and $B\to T$: 5. A cut splits the vertices into a source side containing $S$ and a sink side containing $T$; its capacity is the total capacity of the edges directed from the source side to the sink side. What is the capacity of the cut with source side $\{S,A\}$?

A flow network with source $S$ and sink $T$ has edge capacities $S\to A$: 4, $S\to B$: 3, $A\to B$: 2, $A\to T$: 3 and $B\to T$: 5, with flows nonnegative, within capacity and conserved at $A$ and $B$. What is the maximum flow value?

In a flow network with source $S$ and sink $T$, a cut puts $S$ on a source side and $T$ on a sink side; its capacity is the total capacity of the edges directed from the source side to the sink side. Why does no feasible flow have a value above the capacity of any cut?
options: Because edges from sink side to source side reduce the flow.
All flow reaching $T$ must cross from source side to sink side.
Because the cut contains every edge of the network.
The bound holds only for the cut with the smallest capacity.

questions.question: For a flow network with source $S$ and sink $T$, a feasible flow of value 7 has been found, together with a cut (source side containing $S$, sink side containing $T$) whose edges from source side to sink side have total capacity 7. What follows?
options: The flow is maximum, but a cut of smaller capacity may exist.
Nothing yet; a larger flow with other edge flows may exist.
The flow is maximum only if it is the only flow of value 7.
The flow is maximum, and no cut can have a capacity below 7.

questions.question: In a maximum flow problem, two feasible flows differ on several edges but both send 9 units out of the source, which is the largest possible value. Which statement about these two flows is correct?
options: Only one can be optimal, so one of them must be infeasible.
They must agree on every edge, so they are in fact the same.
Both are optimal only if all capacities are equal.
Both are optimal; a maximum flow need not be unique.

questions.question: Edges $S\to A$, $S\to B$, $B\to A$, $A\to T$, $B\to T$ of a network from source $S$ to sink $T$ have capacities 6, 2, 3, 4 and 5. The vertices are split into $\{S,A\}$ and $\{B,T\}$; the cut capacity counts the edges directed from $\{S,A\}$ to $\{B,T\}$. Which value is this cut capacity?

A flow network with source $S$ and sink $T$ has edge capacities $S\to A$: 3, $S\to B$: 4, $A\to T$: 4, $B\to A$: 2 and $B\to T$: 1, and flow must be conserved at $A$ and $B$. How many units can at most be sent from $S$ to $T$?

In a flow network, $x_{ij}$ is the flow and $c_{ij}$ the capacity of edge $i\to j$. The intermediate vertex $C$ has incoming edges $A\to C$, $B\to C$ and outgoing edges $C\to D$, $C\to T$. Which constraint expresses flow conservation at $C$?
options: $x_{AC}+x_{BC}\le x_{CD}+x_{CT}$
$x_{AC}+x_{BC}=x_{CD}+x_{CT}$
$x_{AC}+x_{BC}=c_{CD}+c_{CT}$

questions.question: In a flow network, a feasible flow of value $v$ and a cut of capacity $v$ are known (capacity = total capacity of edges from the cut's source side to its sink side). The capacity of one edge that does not run from source side to sink side is then raised. What happens to the maximum flow value?
options: It stays $v$, as the cut's capacity is unchanged.
It rises by the amount of the capacity increase.
It may rise if the current flow uses that edge.
It may fall, since the old flow becomes infeasible.

questions.question: A maximum flow problem makes the total outflow of the source $S$ as large as possible, with $x_{ij}\ge0$, $x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$ and conservation at vertices other than $S$ and sink $T$. Suppose edges $S\to A$ and $A\to S$ (capacity 5 each) and $S\to T$ (capacity 1) were allowed. Why does this show the need for the rule that $S$ has only outgoing edges?
options: It shows nothing; with an edge into $S$ the maximum is still 1.
Conservation at $A$ would fail, so the flow would be infeasible.
Flow could circle $S\to A\to S$: outflow 6, but only 1 reaches $T$.
Edge $A\to S$ would need negative flow, which is not allowed.

questions.question: A flow network with source $S$ and sink $T$ has capacity 1 on each edge $S\to A$, $S\to B$, $A\to B$, $A\to T$, $B\to T$. A planner sends 1 unit along $S\to A\to B\to T$; now every route from $S$ to $T$ has a full edge, so no flow can be added along any route. What is the maximum flow value?

A flow network with source $S$ and sink $T$ has capacities $S\to A$: 5, $S\to B$: 4, $A\to C$: 3, $A\to B$: 2, $B\to D$: 5, $C\to T$: 4, $D\to C$: 2, $D\to T$: 4, and a feasible flow of value 8 is known. A cut's capacity is the total capacity of edges from its source side (containing $S$) to its sink side. Which source side gives a cut proving 8 is maximum?
